Area moment of inertia calculator

Area, second moments of area, section moduli and torsion constant of common cross-sections.

How it works

The second moment of area I = ∫y²·dA measures how well a cross-section resists bending. Material far from the neutral axis counts most, which is why I-beams and tubes are so efficient.

Key points

  • For a rectangle I = w·h³/12. Height counts cubed, so a beam laid flat is much weaker.
  • Bending stress σ = M/W, with section modulus W = I/e and e the distance to the outer fibre.
  • Bending about the weak axis (smallest I) governs buckling.
  • The torsion constant J_T equals the polar moment only for circular sections. Open sections have a very small J_T.

Assumptions

  • Homogeneous material
  • Bending about the centroidal axes
